items.title: C3 health hooks: wire opencode-working into lane launchers and aggregator ticks (#9571)
items.body: Refs #9571. Queue task 20915 (slice after merged #12077). ## What Wires the `opencode-working` C3 health hook into the two places the design names as failure-to-connect callers that exist in this tree: - **Lane launch.** `opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (`fire_opencode_working_hook`) fires `caller=lane-launch` when the cap step cannot read OpenCode sessions, on the scheduled fire path. `opencode-claimant/launch_one.py` `launch()` fires it on the same condition. `preflight` stays read-only and does not fire. - **Aggregator tick.** `aggregator/src/sources/live.ts` takes an opt-in `onLaptopUnreachable` and calls it when the laptop OpenCode session map fails (already throttled by the existing 15 s failure cache). `aggregator/src/server.ts` passes `fireOpenCodeWorkingHook` (new `health-hook-fire.ts`, one in-flight hook per aggregator process, fire-and-forget). The hook itself is unchanged: it probes read-only, dedupes on its open incident, and records through the existing alert throat. ## Not in this PR (remains open on #9571) - Incident/recovery records as a dedicated `AuditEvent` (`kind = health-hook-incident`) in the events stream. The current runner writes the JSONL file and the `stackHealth` alert POST only. This needs the events-stream append from the design's "Event-store append" section and is not done here. - Slice D: real failure + recovery cycles, C6/C8 shape verification, and the 14-day cutover test. A follow-up task is to be enqueued for #9571. - Live-caller routing for PM-stack surfaces (not wired). ## Verification - `pm-stack/opencode-claimant`: `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s . -p 'test_*.py'` → 240 OK. The cap-unknown test now patches the new helper and asserts one `lane-launch` call. Offline tests forbid subprocess, so the real hook is never spawned from tests. - `pm-stack/health-hooks`: `PYTHONPATH=. uv run --with pytest pytest -q test_run.py` → 22 passed (unchanged). - `pm-stack/aggregator`: `bun test test/laptop-map-cache-5082.test.ts test/health-hook-dispatch.test.ts` → 6 pass. - `tsc --noEmit` could not run in this environment (missing `bun` type package, error TS2688 before type-checking). Typecheck is unverified; CI should cover it. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added health-hook notifications when OpenCode session availability cannot be determined, including during aggregator checks and task launches. * **Documentation** * Clarified when health hooks are triggered and which parts of PM-stack do not invoke them.

items.title: feat(aggregator): report quota extractor health (#1204)
items.body: ## Summary ```text quota-view extractors ├─ pools: matched / gap / intentional + window count └─ services: matched / gap / intentional + metric count ├─> /api/quota.json.extractorHealth └─> visible “extraction gap” badges on affected quota cards ``` Older feeds report `unavailable`; intentional shell pools and uninstrumented services are not flagged as gaps. ## Evidence - **Before:** a missing section or failed parse produced a healthy-looking empty shell with no diagnostics. - **After:** tests distinguish section-missing, extractor-null, and extractor-threw; intentional shells remain unflagged. - Focused tests: `bun test test/quota.test.ts test/usage.test.ts test/quota-contract.test.ts` — 76 passed. - Full aggregator suite: 918 passed; one `test/slice3.test.ts` failure was reproduced on clean `main`. Typecheck reports existing errors in `push.ts` and unrelated tests, with none in changed files. ## Merge Danger **Door:** Two-way; revert restores the prior quota payload and cards. **Blast Radius:** Low — additive diagnostics and quota-card badges only. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Quota and service cards now display an extraction-gap indicator when usage data could not be extracted. * The quota API now includes extraction health details, showing whether data matched, had a gap, was intentionally uninstrumented, or was unavailable. * **Bug Fixes** * Extraction results now distinguish between missing data, unsuccessful matches, and extraction errors, improving the status information shown for quota and service data.

items.title: fix(route-proxy): provider_routes expansion + built-in endpoint defaults (#3256)
items.body: Fixes #3256 (both work items: the provider_routes grammar the deployed config collapsed to on 2026-11-01, and the GPT door behind it). ## Repro (before this fix, unfixed proxy on a scratch port against the deployed config, scratch DB) - Walk on `luna-plan` and on `terra-plan` (whose only target is `openai-plan/gpt-6.1-terra`): route_attempt row `('terra-plan', 'openai-plan', 'gpt-6.1-terra', 'failure', 'UnknownProvider', 'no endpoint configured for provider openai-plan', session_id NULL)` — the group id was treated as a concrete leaf provider. - Walk on a route with explicit GPT leaves (added to a *copy* of the deployed config, no live config change): `('repro-openai', 'openai.alternate', 'gpt-6-luna', 'failure', 'UnknownProvider', 'no endpoint configured for provider openai.alternate', NULL)` and the same for `openai` — matching ledger rows 41997/41998 cited in #3256. ## Fix — `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` only (single file, no new deps) **(a) Provider routes.** The proxy now parses `experimental.provider_routes` (fallback: top-level `provider_routes`) and expands a `/` target inline at its position in the consuming route's target list, so the consuming route's own selection/weights apply to the group target as written (e.g. luna-plan's weight 2.5 on `openai-plan/gpt-6-luna`), consistent with nested-route expansion. Group selection follows the fork's PR #1134 semantics: `ordered` = member order; `round-robin` = rotation per group+model; `weighted` = weighted draw with the group's weights keyed by member provider id, re-keyed to `/`. Member rules mirror the fork v1: a concrete provider always wins a reference (an id naming a config/built-in provider is never a group), duplicates drop, members naming another provider route or `opencode-route` drop (no nesting), unknown members contribute no leaves, disabled members are skipped, and a member whose effective models map (instanceOf chains included) does not offer the target model is skipped for that dispatch. `#variant` threading, window gates on the group target, quota demotion, and NULL-session attempt rows are unchanged (demotion/attempts key on the concrete member). **(b) Built-in endpoint defaults (issue option 2).** `BUILTIN_PROVIDERS` is now a defaults table merged *under* each config provider block (`mergedDef`): config fields win key by key, the table only fills what a block omits, so an empty-shell block is no longer a dead leaf. Endpoint sources — fork `developing-today/opencode`, `packages/ai`: `openai` = `https://api.openai.com/v1` (`src/protocols/openai-chat.ts` `DEFAULT_BASE_URL`; the models.dev catalog entry for `@ai-sdk/openai` carries no api URL, so the SDK default is the catalog default); `deepseek` = `https://api.deepseek.com/v1`, `groq` = `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`, `openrouter` = `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, `meta` = `https://api.meta.ai/v1` (the `baseURL` constant in `src/providers/.ts` of the same package). `openai.alternate` needs no entry: it is `instanceOf: openai` and inherits the default through the base block. The existing `opencode-go` entry is unchanged. **Companion fix in `credentialKey`:** the credential store holds `{key}` for API providers but `{access}` for OAuth credentials (both GPT plan providers). Without reading the OAuth shape, GPT leaves would still die locally with "no credential" before reaching the now-resolved endpoint; the member's stored bearer is now whichever shape the store holds. No credential values are logged or recorded. **Validation coverage (issue AC3):** there is no separate route-validation script for the proxy's view in this repo; the proxy's test suite is that surface, and it now covers the proxy's view of both hazards (group targets and empty-shell provider blocks), so a config edit that empties a provider block or seats a group target is caught by `bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs`. ## Tests `node --test bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs` — 16 tests, 16 pass, 0 fail (11 pre-existing + 5 new): ordered group expansion (attempt recorded under the concrete member, never the group id), round-robin group rotation, weighted group (weights keyed by member id), member skipped when its catalog lacks the model, and empty-shell `openai` block resolving the built-in default (network-free: endpoint is checked before credentials, so resolution surfaces as a credential failure, not UnknownProvider). ## Live verification Pending at first push; results will be posted as a PR comment (fixed proxy on a scratch port against the deployed config + the real ledger, walking a GPT group route; production :18750 untouched). --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Provider routes can now use groups of eligible providers, with ordered, round-robin, or weighted selection. Providers without the requested model are skipped, and route behavior is preserved. * Built-in endpoint defaults are available for several providers, including when their configuration is otherwise minimal. * **Bug Fixes** * OAuth credentials with an access token are now accepted, even when no API key is provided.
